Keeps the on-device Cox server running
Open the last used server when the app starts
Remembers the server and page you had open. Starts the local server first if it isn\'t running.
Keep screen on while the local server runs
Only while CoCode is in the foreground. Leaving the app lets the screen sleep normally.
Installs a small Linux system on this phone and runs Cox with your coding agents inside it. Your projects and sessions stay on the device.
Alpine Linux, Node.js, Git, the servers you pick and agent CLIs
About 1.2 GB to download and store
Takes a few minutes and keeps going in the background
That may not be enough space.
You can leave the app. Setup keeps going in the background and shows its progress in a notification.
%1$s is installed. Start the server to open it.
Repair reinstalls the Linux system. Your projects are kept when possible.
Running a server on the device needs an ARM64 (arm64-v8a) or x86_64 phone or tablet. You can still connect to a Cox server on your computer below.
Choose at least one agent. CLIs are installed on PATH; Cursor uses the SDK included with Cox.
Select at least one coding agent.
Checking an agent installs it next to the ones you have. Unchecking an installed agent and tapping Apply uninstalls it.

Only the agents you unchecked are uninstalled; adding an agent never removes another. Their settings and sign-ins in the home folder and your projects are kept, so you can check them again later. The local server restarts if it is running.
Cox is unavailable until the update is done. You can leave the app. The update keeps going in the background and shows its progress in a notification.

Cox stops during the update and starts again afterwards, so running tasks are interrupted. The update downloads up to a few hundred MB and takes several minutes. Projects and settings are kept, and if anything fails, the current version keeps working.
The update downloads up to a few hundred MB and takes several minutes. Cox can\'t start until it\'s done. Projects and settings are kept, and if anything fails, the current version keeps working.
The current version is still installed and works as before.

Keep projects, the OpenCode settings, Codex config and the Claude Code folder in CoCode/ on your phone\'s storage, so you can open them with a file manager or over USB. Claude Code is shared in full, including sign-ins and session history. Codex shares only its config; its sign-in and sessions stay inside the app.
CoCode needs all-files access to use this folder. You can turn it on in system settings.
CoCode needs access to your phone\'s storage to use this folder.
Other apps with all-files access can read this folder.
Other apps with storage access can read this folder.
Codex config (config.toml, AGENTS.md, skills, rules, prompts); sign-in and sessions stay inside the app
All of Claude Code, including the sign-in (.credentials.json) and sessions
Claude Code sign-ins and session history are in this folder. File managers and other apps with storage access can read them and use your account. Codex sign-ins and sessions stay inside the app.
Kept inside the app: ~/.codex (Codex sign-ins, locks and sessions), ~/projects-private, ~/.claude.json, OpenCode sessions (~/.local/share/opencode), OpenCode\'s service password and node_modules.
Share the Claude Code folder and Codex config, including Claude sign-ins?
These folders on your phone\'s storage become the shared folders: codex/ holds only Codex config linked from ~/.codex; claude/ is the real ~/.claude.

The Claude Code folder is shared in full: its login credentials (.credentials.json), sessions and history are stored there. Codex shares only config files; its auth.json, locks and sessions stay inside the app. File managers and other apps with storage access can read the Claude data, copy it and use your account.
Your current Codex config and Claude Code settings/sign-ins are copied there once; nothing inside the app is deleted. Turning this off later doesn\'t copy changes back.
I understand that other apps can read my Claude Code sign-ins and sessions

Turning this on puts Claude Code sign-ins and session history in this folder. Codex sign-ins and sessions stay inside the app. File managers and other apps with storage access can then read the Claude data and use your account.
Codex config and Claude Code aren\'t shared yet

Only projects/ and opencode/ are shared. This version can also share Codex config and the full Claude Code folder, including Claude sign-ins and sessions. Codex sign-ins and sessions stay inside the app. Nothing changes until you agree.

Kept inside the app: ~/.codex (Codex sign-ins, locks and sessions), ~/.claude, ~/projects-private, ~/.claude.json, OpenCode sessions (~/.local/share/opencode), OpenCode\'s service password and node_modules.
Your files stay in CoCode/ on your phone\'s storage; nothing there is deleted or copied back. From the next server start, projects and OpenCode settings come from the app again.
CoCode has access, but can\'t create CoCode/ on your phone\'s storage. Make sure the storage is available.
Shared storage doesn\'t keep symlinks or executable bits — use ~/projects-private for projects that need node_modules.

Everything stays in CoCode/ on your phone\'s storage; nothing there is deleted or copied back. From the next server start, Codex config links are restored to the in-app copies and Claude Code uses its in-app copy again. Codex sign-ins and sessions were always in the app; Claude\'s in-app copy may be out of date, so you may need to sign in again and newer Claude sessions/settings are only in CoCode/.
This stops the local server, deletes the Linux system and installs it again with the servers and agents you picked, which downloads about 1.2 GB. Your projects are kept when possible.
This stops the local server and deletes the Linux system from this phone, including both servers, projects, sessions and settings stored inside it. Saved servers are not affected.

This stops the local server and deletes the Linux system from this phone, including everything stored inside it, such as the Codex sign-in and sessions. The CoCode/ folder on your phone\'s storage is kept, including the Codex config and the Claude Code sign-ins and sessions in it. Saved servers are not affected.
Add the address of a Cox server on your computer or network, for example 192.0.2.20:3773.
The saved address, password and this server\'s website data are deleted from this phone. The server itself isn\'t changed.

Checking Node.js, Cox and the agent CLIs
Not enough free space to update. The update needs a temporary copy of the Linux system.
A newer version of CoCode has been released. Download the APK from the release page and install it over this one; your servers, projects and settings are kept.
Configure model service URLs, API keys, protocols and models in Cox, then bind them to your agents. Agent installation and authentication are managed in Cox.
Cox starts automatically when needed. Cursor uses the bundled SDK. Antigravity and ACP agents use Cox installers; Fx and Muse require an executable configured in Cox.
Set up Cox first. Settings are available when setup or maintenance finishes.
Update Cox to 0.1.21 or newer using Check for updates in Details to use the model center. Agent settings are still available.
